title: Logical Connectives
body:
Sentential logic builds compound statements from simple ones using five **connectives**. Each
is truth-functional, meaning the truth value of the compound is fixed by the truth values of
its parts, with nothing else contributing.

| Name | Symbol | English | True when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Negation | ¬P | not P | P is false |
| Conjunction | P∧Q | P and Q | both are true |
| Disjunction | P∨Q | P or Q | at least one is true |
| [[Material Conditional]] | P→Q | if P then Q | P is false, or Q is true |
| Biconditional | P↔Q | P if and only if Q | both have the same value |

```
 P  Q | ¬P | P∧Q | P∨Q | P→Q | P↔Q
 T  T |  F |  T  |  T  |  T  |  T
 T  F |  F |  F  |  T  |  F  |  F
 F  T |  T |  F  |  T  |  T  |  F
 F  F |  T |  F  |  F  |  T  |  T
```

Disjunction is inclusive, so `P∨Q` is true when both hold, and English "or" is often meant
exclusively, which the translation has to decide. Truth-functionality is what makes a
[[Truth Table]] possible, and it is also what the connectives give up: "P because Q" is
not truth-functional, since knowing both parts are true says nothing about whether one caused
the other.

These are the AND, OR and NOT of [[Boolean Algebra]] with T and F written for 1 and 0.
